data.narrative:
Rainmaker is a Series A-stage drone and autonomous systems company founded by Augustus Doricko that has raised $25M to date. The relevant peer set in Drones & Autonomous comprises eight private companies, including Waymo, Wayve, Zipline, Joby Aviation, and Nuro; no public comparables exist in this narrowly defined sector at present.

Only one valuation method proved applicable to this engagement. The Stage-Progression approach, which uses total capital raised as a proxy for current valuation and applies a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage step-ups, yields an implied valuation of $50M. A peer-median analysis was not feasible due to insufficient depth: while seven same-sector peers exist, none of the narrow filtering criteria—same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier—produced three or more datapoints necessary for meaningful triangulation. Relying on an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable bias given the heterogeneity of business models and maturity within autonomous systems.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $42M (low) to $57M (high), with a median point of $50M. This range reflects stage-typical progression dynamics but carries material uncertainty. The primary limitation is the sparse comparability set at Rainmaker's specific stage and valuation tier. Resolution of this uncertainty would require either closer visibility into recent funding rounds among same-stage peers or refined operational metrics (revenue, burn rate, unit economics) that might anchor a DCF-based alternative.
